saints.name: St. Wilfrid
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A Northumbrian bishop who championed the customs of Rome and carried the faith to the pagan South Saxons…
biography: Born in Northumbria about 633, Wilfrid studied at Lindisfarne and Rome and became a forceful advocate of Roman usages against the older Celtic traditions of the North. At the Synod of Whitby in 664 his argument helped persuade King Oswiu to adopt the Roman method of calculating Easter, aligning the English Church with the wider West.

As bishop of York he founded monasteries and endured repeated exiles amid disputes with kings and fellow bishops, appealing more than once to Rome. In banishment he evangelized the still-pagan South Saxons of Sussex. He died in 709 and was honoured as one of the great churchmen of Anglo-Saxon England.
saints.knownFor: Championing Roman usages at the Synod of Whitby.
